text:
marta: Quick alert from intake: about 1.7% of HubSpot leads are landing with owner=null during the enrichment spike window. This is creating duplicates and routing gaps. Can we draft a minimal operational playbook to avoid customer-facing delays?

sam: Thanks for flagging. Do we know if this is from the enrichment timeout, webhook retries, or our RR claimant collisions?

ryan: I traced a sample: HS webhook 429s + enrichment downstream queue backpressure. The assigner currently waits synchronously for enrichment up to 45s, then marks as unassigned. That window is causing 2 failure modes: 1) lead created w/o owner, 2) duplicate create attempts when retry logic kicks in.

marta: Noted. Proposal summary: 1) move to optimistic assign (fast-path) with fallback owner `inbound-marketing-hold` 2) short-circuit enrichment wait to 8s for primary path 3) fallback leads go to a dead-letter queue for manual triage + auto-backfill process 4) make RR resilient to collisions via 20s jitter + owner token lease.

sam: For SF interactions: ensure any inbound create rule doesn't null our owner. Also we should tag fallback leads with `fallback_reason=ENRICH_TIMEOUT` so SalesOps can filter.

opsbot: lead-monitor: 12 unassigned leads >10m in last 12h, peak 09:00-10:00 PDT.

ryan: Implementation sketch: add `fast_assign=true` flag to assigner. If enrichment completes later, merge enrichment fields into existing lead record instead of creating new owner. Add idempotency key on HS webhook to avoid duplicate creates.

marta: Sounds good. Add metrics we care about: assign_p50/p95, fallback_rate, duplicates_blocked, dsync_applied. Also set alert: fallback_rate > 1% over 10m -> page on-call.

sam: Quick config snippet (staging):
```json
{"assigner": {"fast_assign": true, "enrichment_wait_ms": 8000, "fallback_owner": "inbound-marketing-hold", "idempotency_ttl_s": 300}, "rr": {"jitter_s": 20, "lease_s": 60}}
```

ryan: We'll also add a small migration to owners table: `lease_expires_at` + `is_available` logic. Claim flow becomes: reserve lease -> if claim fails release -> jittered retry. This reduces racing.

marta: Runbook steps for ops: 1) Toggle `fast_assign` flag via feature flag console (FF key `lead.fast_assign`) 2) Watch Grafana panel (Assign latency, fallback_rate, duplicate_creates) 3) If >1% fallback_rate -> rollback flag and open LEAD-900 ticket 4) Manual backfill play: run `backfill_leads --source=deadletter --owner=round-robin` in maintenance window.

opsbot: deploy-bot: staging deploy scheduled 2026-06-13T15:10:00Z (pipeline #459).

sam: QA checklist before prod: a) simulate HS 429 storm in staging b) validate idempotent webhook behavior c) confirm fallback owner visible in Salesforce and not overwritten by automations d) run load test for RR collisions.

ryan: I'll add unit tests for idempotency + an integration test that simulates enrichment delayed by 30s and ensures merging occurs without duplicate create. Also creating a smoke job to reconcile dead-letter leads every 5m.

marta: Rollout plan: enable `fast_assign` in staging -> run 2h chaos window -> if fallback_rate < 0.5% and duplicates blocked > 95% success, enable canary in prod (10% traffic) -> monitor 1h -> full rollout. I'll draft the Confluence playbook and link to dashboards.

salesforce-bot: sf-sync: created ticket SF-402 to review create rules and visibility for fallback owner.

marta: Thanks team. Action items: @ryan implement patch + tests + deadletter backfill job; @sam own SF checks and QA; I'll own rollout + docs + dashboards. Post updates here when staging deploy is green. :thumbsup:
